equipment_type: Indoor air quality sensor and ionizer gateway
applies_to: GPS Air smartIAQ GridSet devices (IAQ sensors, ionizers, fan units) connected to the four ports of a smartIAQ Hub-4 Pro BACnet gateway.
summary: The smartIAQ Hub-4 Pro gateway exposes the GPS Air devices on its four ports as BACnet MS/TP objects. Each port gets up to 32 objects: air-quality readings, filter life, fan airflow and mode, occupancy and ionizer enable. Objects are created when a device first reports, and only for the sensors and actuators that device has. This file lists port 1; ports 2-4 repeat the same objects at 2000, 3000 and 4000.
notes: Instance = port x 1000 + offset, and object names are 'Port <N> <name>'. This file lists port 1 (1001-1061); ports 2, 3 and 4 use 2001-2061, 3001-3061 and 4001-4061 with the same offsets.
Objects are created dynamically when a device first reports on a port. Points with a capability gate (shown in the descriptions) only appear if the device has that sensor or actuator.

The points table marks every object except CO2 Occ Threshold as not writable, but the manual's Writable Objects section says Fan Duty Override, Fan CFM Set point, Fan Mode Command and Ionizer Enable also accept writes; they are listed here as writable.
Motor Run State is printed with the same 1=Auto, 2=Manual states as Fan Mode; Motor Fault has no state text in the table.
All objects support COV. Sensor AIs (offsets 1-12) report COMMUNICATION_FAILURE reliability when the port is down or the sensor data is stale.

integration.summary: Set the gateway's device instance, MS/TP MAC and baud in Bus Manager mode, put the jumpers back, then discover it on the MS/TP trunk. Each connected device shows up as a block of objects at port x 1000. Read the air-quality AIs and filter status, and write fan mode, airflow or duty and the ionizer enable where the device supports them. Check Device Online per port.

minimum_points.name: Port 1 Device Online
minimum_points.why: Device on this port is communicating

integration.enable: No separate enable point. Objects appear once a device reports on a port; ionizer output is switched with Ionizer Enable (BV x050).
setup: Settings are changed in Bus Manager mode: power down, move the jumper from the Spare pins to the Modbus pins, power up and connect point-to-point over RS-485 at 115200 8N1 with a terminal program.
Bus Manager sets device instance, MS/TP MAC, baud, Max_Master, device name, location, description and password; option 11 saves.
The manual's example Bus Manager screen shows device instance 1000, MAC 1, 38400 baud and Max_Master 127.
Disconnect the gateway from the live BACnet trunk while in Bus Manager mode, and restore the jumpers afterwards.
Factory reset (option 13, type RESET) clears a lost password and restores all defaults.
gotchas: Objects only exist for the sensors a device actually has, so object counts differ from port to port.
COV subscriptions are limited to 128 in total and 16 subscriber addresses.
Writable AVs hold a BMS write as pending until the device accepts it, so the reported value may lag.
